papers.summary: We study a canonical scalar field coupled to isotropic triplets of Abelian one-forms and two-forms through scalar-dependent kinetic functions and a constant topological $BF$ interaction. By retaining the lapse in the homogeneous reduction, we recover the Friedmann constraint and identify a sufficient domain in which all twelve physical modes have positive kinetic terms and luminal high-frequency propagation. A separate exponential model admits an accelerating mixed solution with $a\propto t^2$, nonzero asymptotic form fractions, and bounded normalized linear perturbations. For the Noether analysis, we choose a quadratic effective potential in flat minisuperspace coordinates and solve the zero-boundary determining equations. The canonical scalar potential is hyperbolic-squared or exponential, rather than a power law in the scalar field. The causal character of the potential coordinate separates three branches: Branch I admits a de Sitter limit, Branch II cannot sustain acceleration on regular future-complete expanding trajectories, and Branch III gives an exact solution with both form sectors active and late expansion $a\propto t^{4/3}$. Comparisons with consistent uncoupled and reduced-field limits separate the form contributions from the scalar-driven acceleration. The $BF$ term changes the finite-time exchange between the form sectors but supplies no direct negative-pressure source.

papers.title: Where Should the Evaluation Budget Go in LLM-Driven Agent Scaffold Evolution?
papers.summary: Large language model (LLM)-driven agent scaffold evolution improves agent workflows through iterative candidate generation and evaluation. Evaluation both guides subsequent search and determines the final scaffold, but evaluating every candidate on the full task set incurs substantial execution costs. We investigate how evaluation budgets can be allocated across these two roles. Our experiments show that sparse feedback can sustain productive evolution, while additional targeted evaluation improves final selection. Replay analyses further show that shared informative items and a common scoring reference support comparisons among closely matched candidates. Motivated by these findings, we propose \method, an evaluation allocation framework that combines sparse search-time feedback with targeted final confirmation. A short fully evaluated warm-up establishes a shared informative core and calibrates a response model whose item parameters remain fixed during search. After search, \method refits the model and applies paired successive halving, reusing accumulated observations and executing only missing evaluations. Across four benchmarks and two evolution frameworks, \method achieves higher mean performance than full evaluation in most settings while using approximately half as many evaluation cells.

papers.title: A heuristic for optimal coordination of autonomous vehicles: static problems
papers.summary: We consider the coordination of autonomous vehicles at unsignalized intersections, where trajectory planning and crossing-order decisions are intrinsically coupled, thereby making their simultaneous optimization intractable in practice. To this end, we propose a heuristic based on a hierarchical structure consisting of a series of nonlinear programs (NLP) in the lower level, which optimizes trajectories of each vehicle for a given crossing order, and a high-level heuristic to design new crossing schedules that exploits sensitivity information from the lower-level NLPs. Extensive numerical simulations across a broad range of traffic scenarios demonstrate that our strategy achieves substantially improved scheduling with respect to first-in-first-out ordering while preserving computational tractability.

papers.title: An Interactive Mobile Augmented Reality System for Efficient Virtual Model-to-Patient Registration in Thoracic Surgery
papers.summary: Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Surgery (VATS) is a minimally invasive procedure, where precise surgical port placement is vital, yet it relies heavily on surgeon experience and mental mapping of pre-operative imaging in the operating room. To address this challenge, we present an accessible, interactive mobile augmented reality (AR) framework, HILMARTS, to enable accurate and efficient pre-operative virtual model-to-patient registration for AR-guided surgical navigation. Our system runs on a commercially available LiDAR-equipped iPad and supports a user-in-the-loop workflow through a two-stage coarse-to-fine registration process. First, the user performs a manual alignment using the AR view on the iPad. This initial maneuver is then refined through automatic point-cloud registration leveraging the LiDAR sensor. We further introduce a novel occupancy-grid-based Surface Coverage Score to provide real-time, actionable feedback to the operator on the geometric completeness of LiDAR data capture for reliable point-cloud-based alignment. In a phantom study with 16 participants, the system achieved a 3.31+/-1.26mm registration accuracy in ~4 min with a mean System Usability Scale (SUS) of 84.1. These findings highlight the system's accuracy, efficiency, robustness, and potential clinical usability, and could support its applicability to other AR-based surgical navigation tasks.

papers.title: Personal preference or system role? Battery swapping among UK electric vehicle users
papers.summary: Battery swapping replaces a depleted EV battery with a charged one, reducing waiting time and enabling off-peak charging. Evidence on acceptance, however, remains concentrated in Asian markets, and most studies examine individual adoption intentions. This study asks whether current UK EV users judge swapping differently as a purchase option and as a technology for the transport system. Using Behavioural Reasoning Theory, an integrated choice and latent variable model, and latent class analysis, we analyse perceived usefulness, energy-system concerns, practical barriers, and satisfaction with current charging. Usefulness and energy-system concerns relate more strongly to expectations about the system. Battery compatibility and station coverage relate more strongly to personal preference, while spare battery costs relate to expectations about network viability. User groups differ in how they balance benefits, barriers, and satisfaction with existing charging. Policy should address driver barriers and network viability as distinct but connected priorities.

papers.title: Deployed entanglement-based BBM92 quantum key distribution using frequency-converted photons emitted by a quantum dot
papers.summary: Establishing secure communication is an important requirement in existing and future networks. Although current solutions rely on classical approaches, quantum mechanics offers the possibility of moving from computational to information-theoretic security. Quantum key distribution (QKD) has been extensively studied as a means of achieving such security. Recently, epitaxial quantum dots started to be studied and employed in quantum cryptography, because of their rapid development that made them one of the brightest sources of quantum light to date. In particular, they are known to be excellent sources of polarization-entangled photon pairs, especially droplet-etched dots operating at $\sim$780 nm. Here, we employ such a quantum dot to generate entangled photon pairs under 1 GHz excitation rate. Using quantum frequency conversion, we interface the emitted photons with the telecommunication wavelength range while preserving their polarization entanglement. This enables quantum key distribution over a 1.59 km field-deployed fibre link across the University of Stuttgart - campus Vaihingen, using the BBM92 protocol: we achieve a secure key rate of 206 Hz over 19 h of stable operation, resulting in a total secure key length of 14.2 Mbit. This key enables the safe encryption and decryption of a colour image with further implementation of error correction and privacy amplification. These results demonstrate important steps towards hybrid quantum networks by combining high-quality entangled-photon sources operated at high excitation rates, efficient frequency conversion module, and picosecond-level time synchronization in a realistic deployed network.

papers.title: Watermark Basins: Black-Box Detection of Distilled LLMs
papers.summary: Proprietary language models and their reasoning traces are vulnerable to API-based distillation, where an adversary trains a student model on the teacher model's outputs. To obtain evidence of distillation, model providers can watermark the teacher's outputs, aiming to leave a radioactive signal in the student's outputs. Existing black-box detectors search for such radioactivity using token-level statistics of the suspect model's outputs. However, token-level signals are not always detectable, for instance when the distillation traces are sampled at a low temperature. In this work, we discover the watermark basin, a persistent signal that enables more reliable watermark detection: during fine-tuning, watermarked teacher traces embed a distinct, key-specific geometric signal in parameter space that lies orthogonal to the ordinary task-specific fine-tuning subspace. Building on this, we introduce Watermark Basin Alignment (WM-Basin), a black-box watermark detector that queries the suspect model through its API, without access to its weights or logits. WM-Basin maps generated text to gradient representations using a fixed clean probe model, projects out the ordinary fine-tuning task directions, and tests whether the residual gradient aligns with the watermark basin induced by the watermark key. We evaluate WM-Basin extensively across diverse teacher models and student architectures (from 135M to 8.2B parameters) distilled on mathematical reasoning. At a strict 0.1% false-positive rate, WM-Basin detects 79% of distilled models at n-gram=1 and 45% at n-gram=3, substantially improving over the state-of-the-art token-level baseline (29% and 1.3%, respectively). Because the watermark signal resides in a persistent basin, it survives post-distillation modifications including quantization, pruning, and reinforcement-learning post-training.

papers.title: REGLAT at ArGuard Shared Tasks: An Ensemble-Based Model Integrating NER for Harmful Content Detection in Arabic
papers.summary: Detecting harmful content in Arabic is challenging because of dialectal variations and the semantic overlap between different harm categories. This paper presents a two-stage approach for classifying Arabic user prompts into seven categories of harmful content. First, GLiNER is used to extract harm-related entities from each prompt. The extracted entities are then added to the original text and passed to a fine-tuned MARBERT classifier for final classification. The approach combines explicit entity information with the contextual understanding of a pretrained Arabic language model. The system was evaluated on the development set of the ArGuard 2026 shared task. The results achieved a macro-F1 score of 0.886 and an accuracy of 0.897, demonstrating promising performance in fine-grained harmful content detection. The system reported an accuracy of 0.793 and Macro-F score of 0.735 on a blind test set for subtask 1. For subtask 2, it achieved an accuracy of 0.770 and Macro-F score of 0.754. The analysis also showed that distinguishing between related categories remains challenging. These findings suggest that integrating NER with Arabic language models is a promising approach to harmful content detection.
papers.comment: System description paper for REGLAT submission for ArGuard shared task 2026

papers.title: On-shell reduction of spin-zero Duffin-Kemmer-Petiau covariants and implications for the relativistic impulse approximation
papers.summary: We analyze the on-shell content of the local Lorentz covariants of the five-dimensional spin-zero Duffin-Kemmer-Petiau algebra in elastic spin-zero-spin-$1/2$ scattering. The scalar, vector, and tensor structures are reduced explicitly to the two independent amplitudes allowed by the physical parity-conserving process. The two scalar structures are proportional on shell, the genuine nonminimal vector $i[P,β^μ]$ is longitudinal and vanishes after contraction with the conserved fermion vector current, and the projected vectors $Pβ^μ$ and $β^μP$ each reduce to one half of the minimal-vector contribution. The tensor covariants introduce no additional on-shell directions. We discuss the consequences for the four invariant choices used in meson-nucleus optical-potential calculations and show that different nuclear equations can arise only after on-shell-equivalent representatives are promoted to optical operators and iterated beyond the order at which the elementary impulse approximation is fixed. These results provide a systematic basis for distinguishing genuinely independent elementary amplitudes from representation-dependent effects generated by the optical embedding.

papers.title: Precision measurement of the $J/ψ\toμ^+μ^-μ^+μ^-$ branching fraction and search for a new gauge boson $Z^{\prime}$ at BESIII
papers.summary: We present a precision measurement of the branching fraction of the rare decay $J/ψ\toμ^+μ^-μ^+μ^-$, and a search for a new gauge boson $Z^{\prime}$ that couples only to the second and third lepton generations, using a data sample of $(8998 \pm 39) \times 10^6$ $J/ψ$ events collected by the BESIII detector. The branching fraction of the $J/ψ\toμ^+μ^-μ^+μ^-$ decay is measured to be $B(J/ψ\toμ^+μ^-μ^+μ^-)=[0.91\pm0.04~{\rm (stat.)}\pm0.07~{\rm (syst.)}]\times 10^{-6}$, representing the most precise measurement to date and consistent with the theoretical prediction within one standard deviation. Additionally, we search for $CP$ asymmetry in the $J/ψ\toμ^+μ^-μ^+μ^-$ decay and determine the T-odd observable to be $A_T = [0.05\pm 0.04~{\rm (stat.)}\pm0.01~{\rm (syst.)}]$, which is consistent with $CP$ conservation. In the search for $J/ψ\to Z^{\prime}μ^+μ^-$ via $Z^{\prime}\toμ^+μ^-$, no significant $Z^{\prime}$ signal is observed in the $μ^+μ^-$ invariant mass region of $(0.212,~2.6)$~GeV$/c^2$, and we set upper limits on the ${\rm U}(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}$ model coupling constant $g^{\prime}$ ranging from 0.001 to 0.294 at the 90\% confidence level, which is comparable to the upper limits set by Belle II for $Z^{\prime}$ masses below $0.7$~GeV$/c^2$.

papers.title: Your Policy Is Secretly a Harness: The Decision Geometry of Agent Interfaces
papers.summary: Language model agents are post-trained and deployed through a harness, the prompts, tools, and control logic that present a task to the model and execute its outputs. Harnesses are often revised and judged by how an already trained model performs under them, which assumes that what the model learned under one harness carries over to the next. We ask what a policy learns from its harness and what survives when the harness changes. Under KL-regularized control, we show that the log odds of an optimal policy recover how strongly its harness favors each action over the others, so a trained policy carries the preferences of its harness. Deployed return then equals the ceiling of the harness, the best return it offers, minus the mismatch of the policy, the return lost to its own suboptimal decisions. Training changes only the mismatch, while changing the harness moves both terms. Comparing harnesses with a fixed model therefore mixes what each harness offers with how well that model uses it. In MiniWoB++, post-training makes a model's preferences specific to its training harness. Reversing the order of the observation fields leaves every optimal decision unchanged yet lowers a trained model's success from 85.0% to 19.2%. Conversely, every new harness that a fixed-model comparison rejects but that raises the ceiling outperforms the original agent after further training under it, and ceiling and mismatch measured beforehand predict these gains. For coding-agent harnesses on Terminal-Bench Lite, ceiling minus mismatch estimated with a stronger model as a stand-in for the optimum reproduces the accuracy ranking, while either term alone does not. Code is available at https://github.com/2020-qqtcg/HRP.

papers.title: Global Analysis of Nuclear Parton Distribution Functions using Markov Chain Monte Carlo
papers.summary: Global analyses of nuclear parton distribution functions (nPDFs) have traditionally used the Hessian method for uncertainty estimation, relying on a local quadratic approximation of the chi-squared function. This Gaussian approximation can be inadequate when experimental constraints are limited and parameter correlations are strong, as it cannot fully capture asymmetric uncertainties, flat directions, or multiple minima. This thesis develops a Bayesian framework for nPDF determination using Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) techniques within the nCTEQ analysis framework. An adaptive Metropolis-Hastings algorithm enables direct sampling of the posterior distribution, revealing pronounced non-Gaussian behavior and secondary minima, particularly in the valence distributions. The analysis presents the first global single-nucleus determination of lead (Pb) PDFs based exclusively on lead data, complemented by a multi-nuclei analysis incorporating different nuclear targets through a standard analytic dependence on the mass number. Including lighter nuclei significantly constrains quark distributions and changes the extracted lead PDFs, while the gluon distribution remains comparatively stable. A comparison with Hessian-based results highlights the limitations of the Gaussian approximation in regions with strong nonlinearity or multimodality. Overall, this work establishes Bayesian MCMC inference as a flexible framework for nPDF determination, providing a more comprehensive characterization of parameter uncertainties and the underlying parameter space.
papers.comment: PhD thesis, IFJ PAN (Polish Academy of Sciences), October 2026. 211 pages

papers.title: HTM: A Hybrid Classical-Quantum Computation Model
papers.summary: Classical and quantum computers have achieved collaborative computation and completed applications across numerous fields. Nevertheless, the absence of a unified hybrid computation model has led to issues such as non-standardized engineering architecture design, ambiguous task partitioning criteria and so on. To address these issues, this research proposes a hybrid classical-quantum computation model (HTM). By constructing unified state sets and transition function representations, HTM clarifies hybrid control logic and implements a control-sharing mechanism. Simultaneously, a comprehensive complexity calculation method based on entanglement and superposition was proposed, supporting computation task partitioning and resource scheduling. The HTM fills a theoretical gap in the classical-quantum hybrid computation area and implements the joint promotion and development of computing models and hardware.

papers.title: Wavefunction-templated metamaterials
papers.summary: Metamaterials, which store, guide and emit waves through their eigenmodes, have enabled the development of devices with unprecedented functionalities. Yet the spatial profiles of conventional metamaterials' eigenmodes are typically determined by their pre-determined structures (Hamiltonians). In this work, we introduce `wavefunction-templated metamaterials', a class of physically realizable metamaterials hosting diverse prescribed, spectrally isolated eigenstates. The resulting Hamiltonian geometries obey a boundary law, with the required nonlocality determined solely by single-contact boundary sites, independent of the state interior or lattice size. The sparse Hamiltonians are then Hermitianized, followed by spectral reshaping to open a protective gap around the target eigenstate. We validate our approach in discrete lattices and acoustic metamaterials. Although demonstrated in acoustics, the principle can be applied to thermal, electrical-circuit and photonic metamaterials.

papers.title: Quantum circuits of elastic wave equations via Schrödingerisation
papers.summary: We construct explicit quantum circuits for the velocity-stress formulation of elastic wave equations in homogeneous media using Schrödingerisation. After rewriting the equations in symmetric matrix form(SMF), we use Fourier spectral discretization for source-driven periodic problems and staggered-grid finite differences for Dirichlet, Neumann, and impedance boundary conditions. The Schrödingerisation method transforms any linear PDEs into a system of Schrödinger-type PDEs -with unitary evolution- using the warped phase transformation that maps the equations in one higher dimension. For periodic problems, we develop circuits by combining controlled Fourier-mode rotations. For physical boundaries, interleaved encoding swaps the spatial and field-component registers, enabling a more efficient circuit construction using shift operators. We analyze $p$th-order Trotter-Suzuki formulas and derive splitting-error and CNOT-gate estimates, under the assumptions of smooth auxiliary initialization and solution-state recovery. Comparison with classical partitioned splitting methods identifies a polynomial improvement in spatial-resolution dependence for the quantum state-evolution subroutine. Noiseless circuit simulations of a forced periodic problem and an impedance problem illustrate the constructions and quantify their errors against exact solutions and classical reference computations.

papers.title: Aligning Large Language Models for Safety in African Languages: A Case Study of Hausa
papers.summary: Safety alignment research for large language models (LLMs) remains concentrated on high-resource languages, leaving open how existing alignment methods perform in low-resource, culturally distinct settings. We study this question for Hausa, a language spoken by more than 200 million people across West Africa. We introduce HausaSafeLM, one of the first Hausa safety preference dataset, built from 10,000 prompts derived from PKU-SafeRLHF: 3,000 human-corrected (gold) and 7,000 machine-translated (silver) examples spanning six harm macro-categories. Using Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, we compare supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and SFT followed by Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) under both data regimes, evaluating on 500 harmful and 200 benign Hausa prompts.We find that the untuned base model appears highly safe by refusal-rate metrics alone, but this reflects limited Hausa generation ability rather than genuine alignment: its refusals are almost uniformly low quality. SFT improves both refusal fluency and precision and benefits substantially from the larger, noisier silver-tier data, while DPO sharpens refusal precision but comes at a steep, largely data-invariant cost to linguistic quality. No single configuration jointly maximizes safety, helpfulness, and fluency. Our results suggest that current alignment techniques teach models when to refuse more readily than how to do so fluently in underrepresented languages, and that refusal-rate metrics alone are an unreliable signal of safety in low-resource settings.

papers.title: When Is a Relation Worth Trusting? Manipulation Costs, Exposure, and the Trust Trap in Multi-Relational Graph Learning
papers.summary: Multi-relational graph detectors learn from clean data how much to trust each relation, but an adversary pays a different price to manipulate each relation and each action; taking such costs as given, we ask when using a relation is worse than ignoring it. Our first main result proves that degree gating strictly beats every selection or reweighting of a relation when part of the population is isolated on it and the attacker cannot afford to open the gate, and that this window is sharp; on real graphs, validated gating gains exactly on the relations that meet these conditions and nowhere else. Our second shows that a per-node exposure bound, which extends to message passing, tells a platform which relation to harden: exposure per unit cost, computed without any attack, picks the relation whose hardening raises the exact trap threshold most in 15 of 16 cases, against at most 7 for informativeness, cheapness, or an analysis with equal edit costs. Supporting tools give exact worst cases for linear relational models, certified brackets for R-GCN and tree ensembles, and a finite-sample guarantee for adversarial validation, under which clean-trained graph detectors fall below their graph-free counterparts in 58 of 90 settings on six graphs. A selection protocol built on these results is never significantly worse than ignoring the graph; with at most four relations it mostly abstains, as validation alone would, and its cost-aware proposals help when relations are many, so far shown on synthetic graphs. Without cost information, the safe choice is to abstain.

papers.title: Peers4U: Designing Learner-Centered Virtual Peers for Children's Multimodal Mathematics Learning
papers.summary: In early mathematics, children learn abstract concepts through concrete representations, such as manipulating objects, drawing, and speaking. Learning with peers can enrich this process by exposing children to diverse strategies and enabling them to exchange ideas through interaction. We realized this potential with virtual peers in Peers4U, a multimodal learning system to enhance children's mathematical conceptual understanding. Virtual peers driven by LLMs are personalized to the learner's cognitive level and assigned multimodal solutions with inspectable processes. During learning, peers engage in mixed-initiative interactions by responding, initiating topics, and advancing discussions along a pedagogical progression. A user study with 22 children and two experts showed our learner-centered topic orchestration significantly outperformed a persona-centered baseline, and children spontaneously authored new artifacts to demonstrate inspired ideas or share their own strategies, producing significantly more solutions when grouped with more Leading Peers. We contribute design insights for multimodal, learner-centered virtual peer systems.

papers.title: Penalized Cause-Specific Hazard Regression under Competing Risks: An Elastic Net Approach Using SANAD Trial Data
papers.summary: Competing risks analysis is an important framework for studying time-to-event data in the presence of multiple, mutually exclusive events. Traditional methods, such as non-parametric estimators and proportional hazards models, may not adequately capture complex hazard patterns or provide stable estimates in practical settings. In this study, we propose a parametric approach based on the generalized exponential regression model for competing risks data. The model allows flexible hazard shapes and incorporates covariate effects through a regression structure. To improve estimation stability, we integrate elastic net regularization into the likelihood framework. The proposed method is evaluated through simulation studies and applied to a real dataset. The results indicate that the elastic net approach provides more stable and precise estimates compared to standard maximum likelihood estimation. Overall, the proposed framework offers a flexible and practical approach for analyzing competing risks data.

papers.title: Asynchronous Verifiable and Complete Secret Sharing: From Design Patterns to System-Level Trade-offs
papers.summary: Modern secret sharing protocols promise robust secret sharing in fully asynchronous Byzantine systems, but their practical costs remain difficult to compare across papers, assumptions, and workloads. The difficulty is not merely experimental: protocols with similar asymptotic guarantees often place very different work on the critical path through their choices of dissemination, verification, batching, and recovery. This paper turns that fragmented research landscape into a corpus-backed designspace analysis and systems evaluation of asynchronous verifiable and complete secret sharing. We derive a design sieve, select seven representative protocols, and implement them in a common Rust framework. In our experiments on the Grid'5000 platform, we evaluate honest-dealer and faulty-dealer stress executions using latency, throughput, message count, bandwidth, and aggregate CPU-time. The results show that message complexity alone poorly predicts latency, that optimistic paths can be dominated by recovery cost, and that batching or packing helps only when verification stays off the critical path. These findings turn protocol-by-protocol comparisons into design-to-cost guidance for choosing, implementing, and extending asynchronous verifiable and complete sharing protocols.

papers.title: Enhancing magneto-optical coupling and scattering from magnetic vortices by optical polarization texturing
papers.summary: Magnetic textures offer a route toward photonic functionality in which electromagnetic fields are controlled not only by material composition and geometry but also by the internal magnetic configuration. Conversely, spatial texturing of these fields is a qualitatively new tool to increase the effective coupling strength to magnetic matter and to act on the the vortex topology and magnetic dynamics. Here, we investigate the coupling and scattering of structured electromagnetic fields by a magnetic vortex, focusing on how spatially non-collinear magnetization governs polarization conversion, electromagnetic energy flow, and magnetization dynamics. We develop a spherical rigorous coupled-wave method that incorporates the spatially dependent anisotropic magnetic permeability associated with the vortex texture. The calculations show that the off-diagonal components of the magnetic susceptibility mediate conversion into complementary polarization channels that are absent from the incident field. The generated fields exhibit pronounced spatial localization associated with the vortex magnetization profile and support a nonzero azimuthal component of electromagnetic energy flow. A comparison between linearly and radially polarized illumination reveals an approximately one-order-of-magnitude difference in the scattered fields amplitudes due to polarization texturing, demonstrating the importance of spatial overlap between the incident field and the anisotropic magnetic response. The back-action on the magnetic vortex dynamics is quantitatively demonstrated by numerical simulations for the inverse Faraday effect due to the rectification of structured effective-field excitation. It is shown that polarization textured optical fields can drive vortex-core precession and, at sufficiently strong excitation, reverse the core polarity and chirality on nanosecond time scale.

papers.title: Efficient Bootstrap Calibration of Generalized Posteriors with Importance Reweighting
papers.summary: The learning rate of a generalized posterior governs posterior uncertainty but typically has no canonical value. Generalized posterior calibration (GPC) selects this rate by matching bootstrap-estimated credible-interval coverage to its nominal level, often requiring repeated posterior simulation. We propose GPC via importance reweighting (GPC-IRW), which reuses draws from a reference posterior fitted to the original data across bootstrap resamples and candidate learning rates. For quantile-based intervals of a scalar functional, we express the coverage criterion in terms of bootstrap posterior cumulative distribution functions, avoiding computation of individual bootstrap credible intervals. Safeguards based on importance-weight effective sample size and proximity to coverage-decision boundaries invoke reweighting from cached bootstrap-specific draws or direct posterior simulation when necessary. Under the stated regularity conditions, with numerical error tending to zero, we show that median-centered calibration preserves the first-order learning-rate target and achieves asymptotically nominal coverage. The approach extends to independent clusters through cluster-level resampling. Simulations yield coverage and interval lengths comparable to those of existing GPC algorithms at substantially lower computational cost. In an exoplanet mass-radius analysis, GPC-IRW achieves 6.7- and 9.6-fold speedups over MCMC-based calibration in the single-planet and full-sample analyses, respectively, while illustrating the effects of within-host dependence.

papers.title: Decision Models as Judges for Hallucination Detection
papers.summary: Large language models are widely used as judges of model outputs (LLM-as-a-Judge), but they are costly and can hallucinate or be overconfident. Decision models are a potential alternative. They return a predefined verdict with a probability for each label instead of free-form text and are much cheaper and faster. We test this promise on hallucination detection. We build binary benchmarks for five hallucination types (9,852 items from six datasets) and compare five decision models with the generative judge gpt-6-sol. Performance depends strongly on the type: the best decision model matches gpt-6-sol in balanced accuracy on context inconsistency and comes within 3 percentage points on factual errors, but trails it by 4-8 points on logical and instruction inconsistency. Decision-model probabilities are overconfident, though less so than the GPT-6 models, and separate correct from incorrect decisions only moderately. We also find that a confidence cascade of decision models improves on the best single model by 1.9-3.3 points on three types and matches or exceeds gpt-6-sol at 1-3% of its cost. Overall, decision models are a practical low-cost judge for some hallucination types but need to be validated before use.

papers.title: Magnetic crystal generation with site-resolved magnetic moments via Gaussian-mixture retargeting and finite-budget yield prediction
papers.summary: We introduce GMMag, a workflow for generating crystal structures together with their site-resolved magnetic moments, built on a conditional variational autoencoder with a graph neural network encoder and a transformer decoder. Gaussian-mixture sampling redirects generation towards selected chemical and magnetic targets without retraining. We systematically investigate how encoder and decoder design, the representation of magnetic-moment magnitudes and relative signs, and sampling choices affect reconstruction, generation quality and diversity. Because a higher screening pass rate does not necessarily yield more qualifying candidates with distinct chemical formulas absent from the reference dataset, we model how repeated generation of the same chemical formulas limits their accumulation and test the model in two separate ten-million-draw runs. As an application, the workflow identifies Nd-containing candidates with chemical formulas absent from the reference dataset, negative formation energies and high estimated saturation magnetization.
papers.comment: Main text: 28 pages, 8 figures; Supplementary Information: 31 pages, 2 figures (included)

papers.title: Vision-Language-Action or World-Action? Just Action Models
papers.summary: The vision-language-action (VLA) and world-action model (WAM) communities debate whether control policies should inherit pretrained knowledge from vision-language models or from visual generators. The debate, however, bundles three separable choices: backbone initialization, the objective applied to future observations, and whether the machinery for that future loss is kept at inference. A gap between a VLA and a WAM therefore cannot simply be attributed to any one of them. We show that decoupling these choices yields a common framework for both families, which we term Just Action Model (JAM): a pretrained visual backbone with an action expert, trained with an action loss and a foresight loss. The foresight loss trains current-observation features to predict frozen encodings of the recorded future through a prediction head discarded after training, so no visual generation is involved in either training or inference, and the backbone can be chosen freely. We first compare objectives within fixed policy architectures, then evaluate the foresight recipe across backbone families. The resulting JAM policies outperform their matched FastWAM and ImageWAM counterparts on LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus, and achieve similar or slightly higher success rates on RoboTwin. Compared with FastWAM, JAM improves the success rates from 97.0%/55.3%/91.2% to 98.2%/64.5%/91.4%, respectively. With cached foresight targets, JAM reduces estimated online training FLOPs per sample per update by 73% relative to FastWAM. Our results show that future supervision improves control without visual generation or additional inference machinery, and strong foresight performance is attainable with either generator-initialized or vision-language backbones. Project Page: https://y0uroy.github.io/JAM

papers.title: KEPT: Conformal Keepouts Kept in Planning for Enclosed-Space Navigation in Degraded Sensing
papers.summary: Autonomous vehicles in enclosed spaces such as tunnels and mines rely on range maps that smoke, dust and fog make inaccurate. Conformal prediction calibrates a keepout around the mapped walls that covers the true unsafe set at a chosen probability. Typically an unmodified planner treats the keepout as an inflated obstacle, and nothing ensures that the vehicle can stop before the keepout as it moves when sensing degrades. In narrow passages this margin and the planner's buffer close the route, and existing remedies recover reach by relaxing the coverage level. This paper conditions the conformal margin on a label-free severity estimate to hold coverage near its target as degradation varies. A planning and control layer enforces one braking-distance condition on the keepout at plan time and at every command, takes the measured tracking residual as its only margin and never alters the keepout. The keepout is validated on ground-robot smoke recordings and the closed loop in simulated quadrotor flights in a foggy tunnel against the standard deployment. In closed-loop simulation the proposed system substantially reduces entries into the calibrated keepout and reaches numerically more goals than the deployment pattern in both calibration regimes, an observed gain of 3.2 percentage points pooled whose per-regime confidence intervals include zero. The per-class keepout holds its coverage near the target on held-out recordings.

papers.title: Retrieve to Act: Motion Primitive Graph Retrieval for Robust VLA Execution
papers.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies demonstrate remarkable semantic generalization, yet remain highly vulnerable to out-of-distribution (OOD) visual shifts during execution. While existing test-time methods attempt to suppress spurious visual cues, they fundamentally overlook the rich, uncorrupted kinematic priors embedded in the policy's own training experience. We introduce Retrieve to Act (R2A), a test-time scaling framework that formulates OOD robustness purely as a geometric motion primitive retrieval problem. R2A bypasses fragile visual features by structuring successful training demonstrations into an offline spatiotemporal motion primitive graph. During inference, a query-dependent Graph Neural Network dynamically localizes the robot's ongoing execution within this graph, retrieving structurally compatible future motion primitives. These retrieved geometric priors are then seamlessly harmonized with the frozen VLA's predicted actions via a learned, dimension-wise gating mechanism, adaptively rectifying erroneous spatial trajectories while preserving the policy's local reactivity. Extensive experiments across three state-of-the-art VLA architectures, GR00T N1.7, $π_{0.5}$, and StableVLA, demonstrate that R2A consistently and significantly enhances robustness against diverse contextual perturbations. R2A achieves absolute success rate improvements of up to +12% in simulation benchmarks (LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin2.0-Plus) and +40% in real-world deployments, without requiring any finetuning of the base policies. Project page: https://retrieve2act.github.io/r2a/

papers.title: Uncovering Shortcut Amplification in Video RLVR through the Lens of Perceptual Uncertainty Collapse
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has emerged as an effective post-training paradigm for enhancing the video reasoning capability of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs). Despite its empirical effectiveness, we show that outcome-level optimization can introduce an undesirable shortcut amplification effect, whereby models increasingly favor text-prior answers even when they are not supported by the visual evidence. To characterize this behavior, we investigate the training dynamics of video RLVR through the lens of perceptual uncertainty, analyzing how predictive uncertainty evolves under video-conditioned and text-only contexts. Our analysis identifies a perceptual uncertainty collapse phenomenon, in which RL training continuously sharpens the model's answer distribution while the uncertainty reduction attributable to visual evidence progressively diminishes. A further gradient-direction analysis reveals that such confidence enhancement becomes increasingly less aligned with visually grounded uncertainty reduction and is instead dominated by text-prior compression. Motivated by these findings, we propose Bifocal Self-distillation Policy Optimization (BSPO), a self-distillation framework that regulates policy updates with two complementary distributional signals. Specifically, BSPO derives empirical reasoning principles from intra-group correct and incorrect rollouts to identify reasoning-sensitive tokens, and introduces shortcut-aware visual perturbation to penalize predictions that remain invariant when task-relevant visual evidence is weakened. By adaptively reweighting the original RL advantage, BSPO preserves the task-solving benefits of RLVR while promoting updates that are both reasoning-sensitive and visually grounded. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of BSPO in improving video reasoning performance and strengthening visual faithfulness.

papers.title: Magnons in α-Fe2O3 microdisks: from thermal to coherent excitation
papers.summary: Hematite is a prototypical antiferromagnetic insulator for spintronic and magnonic applications, yet controlled studies of coherent magnons in thin films remain challenging due to strain sensitivity and spatial inhomogeneity. Here, we investigate magnon excitations in lithographically patterned hematite microdisks, and obtain reproducible magnon spectra from multiple individual microdisks. Brillouin light scattering reveals bulk-like field-dependent thermal magnon resonances with an ultralow effective damping parameter on the order of ~10-5. Coherent magnons are further excited using a stripline antenna adjacent to the microdisk, revealing a power-dependent frequency blue shift accompanied by a nonlinear evolution of the coherent response under strong microwave driving. Field-dependent analysis indicates a power-dependent increase of the effective magnetic anisotropy field, suggesting a tunable nonlinear response of antiferromagnetic magnons in laterally confined microdisks. These results establish patterned hematite thin films as a platform for exploring coherent and nonlinear antiferromagnetic magnon dynamics.

papers.title: QNETSIM for memory assisted design of satellite and hybrid quantum networks
papers.summary: Space-based quantum information networks require simulation tools that capture orbital dynamics, probabilistic quantum operations, and classical coordination. We introduce QNETSIM, a modular discrete-event simulator for the design and performance evaluation of satellite and hybrid space-ground quantum networks. The framework integrates orbital geometry, free-space optical and fiber channels, quantum memories, entanglement generation, and Bell-state measurements within a common event-driven architecture. Physical models account for optical loss, atmospheric turbulence, detector imperfections, finite memory capacity, and storage-induced decoherence. Space-time routing and segmented nesting support entanglement distribution across changing topologies, while a software-defined control plane coordinates generation, storage, and swapping. Configurable scenarios encompass onboard repeaters, satellite constellations, ground-based repeaters, and direct satellite distribution. Through explicit interfaces between physical models, network protocols, and orchestration, QNETSIM links component characteristics and operational policies to entanglement fidelity, throughput, latency, availability, and memory utilization, enabling systematic exploration of architectural and resource-management trade-offs in future space-based quantum information networks.
papers.comment: This work was carried out as part of the European Space Agency (ESA) project Quantum information NETworks SIMulator (QNETSIM), under ESA Contract No. 40001 49440125/NL/FGL/lf

papers.title: Remember Where You Walk: Learning Spatial Memory for End-to-End Legged Robot Exploration
papers.summary: Humanoids and other legged robots operating in complex environments must remember information that leaves their field of view and only becomes relevant much later. Reinforcement learning policies address this using memory networks such as LSTMs that are trained end-to-end with the policy to memorize such task-relevant aspects. Yet, such architectures often fail to preserve sufficient information over long horizons. In this work, we propose a network architecture based on Hadamard memory that specifically targets robot navigation. Our Local Spatial Matrix Memory (LSMM) enables RL agents to store generic task-relevant information at specific, position-based memory cells, enabling flexible and spatially grounded memorization. We evaluate LSMM on the task of autonomous maze exploration, where it matches the maze coverage of strong recurrent and finite-history baselines while being the only architecture that remembers the maze layout, reducing the reconstruction error threefold.

papers.title: A Bi-level Co-design Framework for Lunar Monoped with 2D Jump and Landing Control
papers.summary: Legged robots for lunar exploration must be designed for low gravity, where reduced contact forces and long flight phases make leg morphology and controller choice interdependent. We study this for a planar monoped in lunar gravity ($1.625$ m/s$^2$) using a bi-level co-design framework: a differential evolution outer loop searches over link lengths, and each candidate is evaluated on a vertical jump by either a quadratic program based task-space controller (QP-TSC) or a direct-collocation based trajectory optimization. The two controllers yield different optimal link lengths, and trajectory optimization outperforms the QP-TSC across most of the design space, with 17% lower Cost of Transport (COT) at their respective optima. We then extend to a 2D jump, where trajectory optimization with centroidal angular momentum regulation produces stable in-place and forward jumps, and an LQR controller absorbs impact and stabilizes the robot after touchdown. This is demonstrated on a baseline morphology with both links 0.3 m long.

papers.title: Thermodynamics and phase structure of rotating Hayward-AdS black holes
papers.summary: We use the modified Newman--Janis algorithm to obtain the rotating ``mother'' black hole solution of the rotating Hayward-AdS black hole. We further derive the fundamental thermodynamic quantities of the ``mother'' black hole in the full unconstrained phase space $(S,J,q,α,P)$, and impose the regularity condition $M_1=q^3/α$ to obtain the thermodynamic quantities of the rotating Hayward-AdS regular black hole. This order of operations gives a Hawking temperature identical to the surface gravity temperature and produces the correct response functions of the regular black hole. For $P<P_c$, the Hawking temperature $T_2$ possesses a local maximum and a local minimum, which divides the black hole into small, intermediate, and large black hole branches, and the $P$--$V$ isotherms display oscillatory behavior characteristic of a liquid/gas phase transition. The small and large black hole branches are locally stable, whereas the intermediate black hole branch has negative heat capacity and is locally unstable. Increasing the rotation parameter $a$, magnetic charge $q$, or pressure $P$ reduces the region of the intermediate branch. The $G_2$--$T_2$ diagram shows that the phase structure, in contrast to the standard swallowtail of the Reissner--Nordström-AdS and Kerr--Newman-AdS black holes, is 8-shaped or C-shaped. These two shapes are divided by the characteristic pressure $P_z$. For $P<P_z$, the curve is 8-shaped, corresponding to a first-order small/large black hole transition. For $P_z<P<P_c$, the curve is C-shaped, corresponding to a zeroth-order transition. These results show that the 8-shaped/C-shaped phase structure characteristic of regular AdS black holes persists under rotation, indicating that it stems from the restructuring of the thermodynamic phase space by the regularity condition rather than from spherical symmetry.

papers.title: Phase Separation in a Mixture System of Active and Passive Particles
papers.summary: We carried out molecular dynamics simulations of a mixture of self-propelled particles (SPPs) and passive particles. When the self-propulsion speed was sufficiently high, the system separated into two phases. One phase consists of ordered passive particles, and the other is a disordered mixture of both particle types. The separation arises from the interplay between the self-propelled motion of SPPs and thermal motion of the passive particles, since phase separation does not appear with either particle type alone. As the self-propulsion speed increases, the SPPs push surrounding particles away, effectively increasing their excluded size. As a result, the increase in the effective excluded sizes promotes the accumulation of passive particles and the segregation of SPPs into the dilute phase through a mechanism analogous to the depletion interaction. This mechanism explains the phase separation observed in the present study. Our findings provide insights into the potential applications of SPPs and contribute to our understanding of natural systems composed of elements with different levels of motility.

papers.title: Estimation and Inference for One-pass Streaming Function-on-Function Regression
papers.summary: In many applications, functional pairs are collected sequentially from a data stream. Existing function-on-function regression methods are primarily designed for batch data, and bootstrap inference has become one of the most popular approaches. However, this procedure may be infeasible when observations cannot be stored. In this paper, we propose a one-pass functional SGD estimator that updates upon each observation's arrival without data storage, and a weighted rolling validation rule is provided for step size selection for implementation. Further, an online multiplier bootstrap is developed for inference that updates perturbed stochastic gradient paths in parallel, bypassing estimating an infinite-dimensional covariance operator. Asymptotic behaviors are established for the proposed method, and conditional bootstrap validity is justified for the bias-centered pointwise estimation error. Simulation studies and two real data applications confirm the empirical effectiveness of the proposed procedures. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first theoretically justified one-pass framework for bootstrap inference on a bivariate coefficient surface with streaming functional data.

papers.title: Negative Results for Reciprocity-Based Over-the-Air Split Learning Under Channel Aging: Stability, Alignment, and Geometry
papers.summary: In reciprocity-based over-the-air split learning, channel aging rotates and attenuates the derivative signal returned to the transmitter. Seven case studies combine numerical forecasts, mechanism checks, and competing predictions. Near the correlation zero, an archived SGD comparison finds truncated inversion 0.000813 lower in cross-entropy than polar correction, with a paired 95% interval for the difference from -0.001853 to 0.000060, and a retained-mode quadratic proxy slightly favors truncation. Selecting the return port with the largest received power falls short of the predicted five-point alignment advantage over random selection at both tested spacings, gaining at most 0.97 points, while the local inverse relation between amplitude and phase gradient is supported. Seven specified interference-induced accuracy-collapse predictions are rejected, and independent zero-mean interference preserves the conditional mean under a fixed linear chain. Per-subcarrier correction and spherical-wavefront compensation do not deliver their predicted accuracy gains. Focusing leaves both methods near chance in a single-mode model and adds no observed gain in a model with a line-of-sight component plus scattering. A successful port assignment under nonsymmetric motion refutes an exact-symmetry requirement. The competing positioning-error prediction is supported. Gaussian rail jitter with a standard deviation of 0.383 wavelengths yields high terminal test accuracy, whereas a fixed bias of the same magnitude yields near-chance accuracy. These cases distinguish valid local physical relations from unsupported training forecasts through task support, noise injection, and update moments.
papers.comment: 10 pages, 1 figure, 5 tables. Companion to arXiv:2610.23118, arXiv:2610.23135 and arXiv:2610.23137

papers.title: Deep Holes and Aperture: Sign Laws for the Empirical Correlation of Lattice-Sampled Random Wave Fields
papers.summary: A Gaussian random wave field is sampled on a lattice within a bounded aperture. After displacement, re-indexing leaves a residual in the Voronoi cell. We study whether the empirical lag correlation has positive real part throughout the cell. For each realization in a single-output reciprocal link with noiseless over-the-air return, this is equivalent to the negative returned gradient being a descent direction for all residuals and differentiable losses with nonzero error signals. Return noise is treated exactly. For isotropic fields, ball-shaped apertures, unshifted lattice points, and dilations approaching the critical covering radius, every minimizer is a deep hole except with exponentially small probability. A Gaussian vector on the deep holes determines the limiting failure probability, with explicit covariance and lattice-independent limiting normalization. Square, hexagonal, simple cubic, and body-centered cubic lattices have two, three, four, and twelve sign classes. At fixed target failure probabilities below the critical limiting value, this covariance determines the exact leading aperture constant. When the margin and target failure probability vanish jointly, that constant is common to lattice shapes within each dimension. A cubic correction yields vanishing relative tail error in a moderate-deviation regime. A non-asymptotic two-sided aperture law has explicit constants. With a Rayleigh-faded specular path and positive diffuse margin, a failure floor occurs at every positive path power exactly when the cosine of its phase change is negative somewhere in the cell. The floor vanishes for all directions exactly when the covering radius is at most a quarter wavelength.
papers.comment: 22 pages, 1 figure. Submitted to the IEEE Transactions on Information Theory

papers.title: An Application of Geometric Riemannian Pricing Algorithm for Valuing Catastrophe Bonds in Incomplete Markets: Market-Consistent Financial Entropy and the Split of Frequency and Severity Risk Premia
papers.summary: This paper presents a framework for pricing catastrophe (CAT) bonds in incomplete markets through Riemannian geometric optimization of financial entropy. We formulate pricing-measure selection as a maximum financial entropy problem on a finite-dimensional manifold of equivalent measures, parameterized by the non-hedgeable market prices of catastrophe frequency and severity risk, with discounting fixed by the default-free term structure. Since unconstrained entropy maximization recovers the physical measure, we incorporate observed secondary-market spreads, both pooled and date by date. For a compound Poisson-generalized Pareto loss model with Wang distortion, we derive closed-form expressions for financial entropy and the Riemannian metric. We show that CAT bond prices depend on frequency and severity premia primarily through the risk-neutral trigger intensity, making the two premia unidentifiable from market data alone; the entropy criterion resolves this ambiguity. Using a hypothetical earthquake CAT bond calibrated to quarterly spreads of Golden State Re II Ltd. (Series 2014-1), we obtain risk-neutral trigger intensities of 6.58 to 10.45 times the physical intensity (9.20 pooled and 18.26 at the end of 2015). The model-implied risk multiple aligns with the market spread-to-expected-loss ratio (8.87 versus 8.81 at issuance). The minimal-entropy measure attributes 53.5% to 63.7% of the log risk multiple to frequency risk, reflecting the selection principle rather than market identification. Finally, equating the coupon with the quoted spread understates the risk multiple by approximately half.

papers.title: Channel-Differentiated Topological Charge Flips and Formation of Janus Bound States in the Continuum in Single-Layer Photonic Lattices
papers.summary: The topological charge of a bound state in the continuum (BIC) can flip when the BIC merges with other polarization singularities or, as recently shown, at band flips. Here, using a coupled-mode analysis, we derive an analytical expression for the topological charge of symmetry-protected BICs in one-dimensional single-layer photonic lattices. The expression captures both merging-induced and band-flip-induced charge flips. We find that, during a band flip, the topological charge of the BIC reverses with the formation of lines of circular polarization that cross at the $Γ$ point. In vertically symmetric lattices, each charge flip occurs simultaneously in the upward and downward radiation channels. Breaking vertical symmetry makes both kinds of charge flips channel-differentiated, creating a parameter interval in which the BIC carries opposite topological charges in the two channels and forms a Janus BIC. We show that Janus BICs also emerge in experimentally accessible one- and two-dimensional silicon-based photonic lattices. Our results link the topological charge of a BIC directly to the band structure and the channel-resolved radiation amplitudes and establish a basis for channel-selective control of polarization singularities.

papers.title: Reconstructing chiral edge states via boundary dissipation
papers.summary: Boundary dissipation can reshape the spatial profiles and decay properties of topological edge modes in Chern insulators. We develop a microscopic boundary-channel framework to explain their decay mechanisms and determine the effective decay rates in the weak- and strong-loss regimes. By retaining the lossy outer orbitals and a normalized edge state of the Hermitian inner system, we identify a directly coupled bright boundary channel, while incorporating the remaining inner states through a Feshbach self-energy. In the Qi--Wu--Zhang model, weak-loss decay is governed to leading order by the original edge state's probability weight on the lossy boundary, with coupling-induced corrections starting at cubic order. At strong loss, the reconstructed inner-edge state instead decays through virtual coupling to the damped bright channel, giving a rate proportional to the squared microscopic coupling and inversely proportional to the bare loss. The Haldane model shows that the same leading decay mechanism holds for a different intercell hopping structure, while additional matrix-valued self-energy feedback modifies the boundary spectrum at finite loss and shifts the exceptional-point threshold. These results provide a unified microscopic description of boundary-state reconstruction and its decay mechanisms, offering testable predictions to guide experiments in photonic crystals, phononic crystals, and topolectrical circuits.

papers.title: Coverage Under Contradiction: A Benchmark for Negation-Aware Retrieval
papers.summary: Coverage-evaluation benchmarks quantify whether retrieved evidence covers the different pieces of information needed to satisfy an information need. Existing benchmarks mostly consider factual claims that may already be known to pretrained retrieval components, leaving open whether retrievers find corpus evidence when it contradicts those priors. We study how retrievers behave when their parametric knowledge and the information in a corpus disagree. To do so, we develop a process to augment a nugget-based coverage benchmark with controlled contradictions. For each nugget, we create a negated counterpart and edit its supporting documents to support that negation while preserving the context. Applying this process to CoverageBench, a benchmark measuring information coverage, we create CoverageBench-Negate, spanning six datasets and roughly 63,000 original-edited evidence pairs (one per nugget-document link). We attach rich construction metadata to every pair and additionally provide out-of-family LLM judgments over all pairs and a human audit of a sample. In baseline experiments, BM25 separates original from edited near-twin evidence substantially better than dense retrievers (Qwen3 and Jina), which stay near chance. We release the benchmark on Hugging Face Datasets (nuggets, documents, pairs) together with the construction materials, including the prompts used to create it.

papers.title: The Disordered Universe 2025: An Intro and a Vision
papers.summary: The Disordered Universe is a novel research direction that exploits ideas and techniques coming from apparently unrelated research areas, ranging from cosmology to scattering amplitudes in particle physics and disordered complex systems, with the aim of addressing open questions in cosmology at all scales, from the very infra-red (or very late time) to the early universe. This paper acts as a general introduction and vision for a set of lectures delivered at the first La Ricotta Summer School "The Disordered Universe 2025", held from 21 July to 10 August 2025. These lectures involved open quantum systems, analytic properties of scattering amplitudes and correlation functions, foundations and quantum aspects of the de Sitter universe, as well as statistical physics out of equilibrium and spin glasses. While the lecture notes related to each course taught at the school will be published separately and are inevitably devoted to both conceptual and technical aspects of each of these topics, the school was not meant to be a collage of independent topics: the present paper has the purpose of outlining the global vision, how cosmology ends up being a unifier and benefits from both their viewpoint and techniques, how all the concepts and techniques originally coming from these four different areas are part of the same cosmological narrative, why this point of view deserves to be explored, and drawing perspectives for the future. We consider it crucial to build a microscopic theory for the early universe and maybe one that embraces all scales.
papers.comment: 29 pages. It merges introduction and conclusion chapters of a book to be published by Springer Lecture Notes in Physics

papers.title: Physics-Guided Flow Matching: A Generative AI Framework for Global Total Electron Content Forecasting
papers.summary: Accurate forecasting of global total electron content (TEC) is important for space weather monitoring and the reliable operation of satellite communication and navigation systems. We propose a physics-guided generative artificial intelligence (AI) framework for day-ahead global TEC forecasting. The framework builds on flow matching, which learns to gradually transform samples from an initial distribution into new samples that share the statistical characteristics of the target data. The proposed model incorporates ionospheric dynamics described by a partial differential equation (PDE) into this transformation process, guiding the changes between initial and target samples using physical knowledge. The model further combines the physical dynamics with statistical patterns captured from data to learn this transformation, adaptively adjusting their relative contributions at each location. The model is trained and evaluated using one year of global TEC data generated by the Thermosphere Ionosphere Electrodynamics General Circulation Model (TIEGCM). The results demonstrate that our model improves both spatial and temporal forecasting accuracy over representative benchmarks, including statistical, deep learning, and generative AI methods at all lead times and across latitudes. The average root mean square error (RMSE) is 39.2% lower than that of ConvLSTM and 23.8% lower than that of the same framework without physical guidance. The learned contribution weights vary systematically with latitude and across geographic locations, showing how the physical contribution changes across the forecast domain. These findings demonstrate that explicit physical guidance improves generative forecasts of global TEC and highlight the value of incorporating physical dynamics into generative AI modeling.

papers.title: What Survives Distillation? A Mechanistic Interpretability Study of GPT-2 and DistilGPT-2
papers.summary: Knowledge distillation compresses large language models into compact students that preserve aggregate metrics, yet the mechanistic consequences of depth-reduction distillation remain largely uncharacterized. This work applies linear CKA, logit lens analysis, attention pattern decomposition, sparse autoencoder feature statistics, and activation patching to compare GPT-2 and its six-layer student DistilGPT-2 across two canonical circuits: the Indirect Object Identification (IOI) circuit and the Greater-Than (GT) circuit. The results reveal a compression-collapse dichotomy: the IOI circuit suffers complete mechanistic collapse (DistilGPT-2: 35.2% accuracy vs. 94.8%, zero name-mover preservation), while the GT circuit survives with 87.7% task performance recovery through active remapping of the teacher's layer-9 comparison head into student layer~4 (mean Pearson r = 0.945). These findings demonstrate that circuit compressibility governs mechanistic survival under distillation, and that aggregate metrics are insufficient diagnostics for circuit integrity.

papers.title: Cu intercalation and field-driven filament formation in vertically aligned MoS$_2$ memristors
papers.summary: Vertically-aligned MoS$_2$ films paired with a Cu top electrode have been used as electrochemical metallization cell memristor devices. The memristive switching has been attributed to the formation of conductive filaments, yet their exact structure has remained elusive. Here we carry out a multi-scale computational study of Cu intercalation, clustering, and field-driven dynamics to eventually model the filament formation under operating conditions. We use density-functional theory results to fine-tune a machine learning force field, and the most important physical phenomena are further distilled into multi-particle kinetic Monte Carlo simulations. By exhaustive enumeration of Cu intercalated structures, we find the most stable structure at MoS$_2$Cu$_{0.11}$ composition, with Cu atoms forming a dice lattice between the MoS$_2$ layers. These structures are shown to exhibit metallic character and can thus form conductive filaments under memristor operation. The simulated switching speed and threshold voltage agree well with the available experimental data. Our results give fundamental insights on the device operation mechanism and guidelines for maximizing switching speed and endurance.

papers.title: EEG-Based Decoding of Musical Mode and Melodic Direction Using Empirical Mode Decomposition
papers.summary: Electroencephalography (EEG) has proven to be a powerful tool for decoding neural activity in real-life scenarios, including the perception and processing of emotions elicited by music. Among the various musical features that modulate these responses, musical mode and melodic direction (or contour) play a central role. This work proposes a novel EEG feature extraction framework based on Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) to decompose EEG signals recorded during active piano performance for the detection of these two musical features. Energy-based descriptors were computed from the first four Intrinsic Mode Functions (IMFs) obtained through EMD and used to train a Wide Neural Network classifier. The model performance was benchmarked against several standard classifiers commonly employed in EEG classification tasks. Two experimental scenarios were explored: intra-subject and intersubject. In the former case, the proposed framework achieved average accuracies of 84%, whereas in the inter-subject case, accuracies reached 81% on average using the first IMF, with AUC-ROC values of 0.9 on average in both cases. A frequency-domain analysis revealed a strong correspondence between the IMFs and conventional EEG sub-bands, except for certain specific frequency components that were not fully represented. Predominant activations were observed over the frontal, temporal, and parietooccipital regions, areas consistently associated with music processing. Furthermore, the proposed method demonstrated robustness to handedness, successfully classifying EEG data across participants regardless of their dominant hand. These findings highlight the potential of EMD-based feature extraction for identifying music-related neural patterns and contribute to advancing research in Music Information Retrieval (MIR), affective neuroscience, and the broader understanding of the neural encoding of musical structure.
papers.journal: S. Guillén, L. J. Tardón, A. M. Barbancho and I. Barbancho, "EEG-Based Decoding of Musical Mode and Melodic Direction Using Empirical Mode Decomposition," in IEEE Access, vol. 14, pp. 119937-119949, 2026

papers.title: Threshold Criteria for Bosonic and Fermionic Trimers on a Square Lattice: A Birman--Schwinger Comparison
papers.summary: We compare two three-particle lattice models on the square lattice at total quasimomentum zero: three identical bosons with attractive contact interactions, and a two-fermion plus one distinguishable particle system with attractive interspecies contact. Using the Birman--Schwinger principle combined with symmetry reduction and strong-coupling asymptotics, we distinguish shared methodology from model-dependent spectral conclusions. For bosons, the ground-state energy behaves as minus three times the coupling plus six minus three over twice the coupling plus higher-order corrections, and exactly two bound states exist below the threshold for large coupling; the second lies at a finite distance 0.03542 below the threshold, a genuine eigenvalue rather than a threshold resonance. For fermions, the critical mass ratio is pi divided by pi minus two, approximately 2.75194; above it, a doubly degenerate level appears at strong coupling. Near onset, the binding energy follows a linear-over-logarithmic law. The results are compared with numerical finite-grid Faddeev computations and with recent three-dimensional classifications of threshold states.

papers.title: Robust PPG-Exclusive Heart Rate Estimation During Maximal Exercise Using Population-Based Priors
papers.summary: PPG is the main technology for wearable heart rate (HR) monitoring. However, motion artifacts during intense physical activity reduce its reliability due to spectral overlap with the cardiac signal. This study investigates whether severely contaminated PPG signals can yield reliable HR estimates without auxiliary sensors by leveraging prior knowledge of HR dynamics. We acquired simultaneous PPG and ECG signals from 21 subjects during a maximal cycloergometer test. Using Leave-One-Subject-Out cross-validation, we built HR evolution priors from the ground-truth ECG and applied Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) to align normalized HR curves and estimate a barycenter average. DTW aligns normalized HR curves with minimal error across all subjects, validating robust population-based priors. For each test subject, we combined the PPG Power Spectral Density (PSD) with the prior distribution to generate a "posterior PSD". We identified and ranked candidate HR trajectories using heuristic search within the "posterior PSD" and selected the most likely path. Our approach reduced mean absolute error (MAE) in BPM relative to the ground-truth ECG by a median of 63.3% (IQR: 47.3%-74.6%) compared to a PPG+accelerometer benchmark. These results show that physiological priors and DTW-based alignment enable robust, PPG-exclusive HR monitoring during high-intensity exercise.
papers.comment: Accepted and presented at 53rd Computing in Cardiology conference in Madrid, Spain on 20th - 23rd September 2026

papers.title: Science-Fiction Transformation as a Design Lens for Visualization Transformation
papers.summary: Science fiction often features characters or objects that undergo radical changes in form while still being recognizable as the same entity. For example, a vehicle might unfold into a robot, or one body might flow or shape-shift into another. We use such transformations as a reflective lens to study similar shape-shifting in visualization, where one visual representation transforms into a completely different one. For example, a node-link diagram might transform into a parallel coordinates plot as a user's task changes from understanding relationships to identifying correlations. Based on four instances of science-fiction transformation, our paper highlights two key questions: First, why is a transformation into a target form needed, or what is the purpose? Second, what remains recognizable across the transformation from source to target, or what is the correspondence? Through four hypothetical transitions between visual representations of a multifaceted dataset, we demonstrate that purpose is also essential to visualization transformations. Furthermore, we show that the question of correspondence results in different levels of complexity in terms of designing and understanding transitions. Depending on whether correspondence is 1:1, 1:N, or N:1, visualization transformations may be direct and easy to understand, or they may require more elaborate transition constructs, implying increased cognitive effort for interpretation. Particularly, cases of 1:N and N:1 correspondence pose challenges for designing visualization transformations.

papers.title: Study of Multilayer TiNx/Ti/TiNx Films Formed In Situ for High-Efficiency Integrated Microheaters
papers.summary: A technology for the in situ formation of a three-layer TiN$_x$/Ti/TiN$_x$ functional material within a single vacuum cycle is presented, together with the results of investigations of its structural and electrophysical properties. The maximum critical power density reached approximately 140 MW/cm$^2$. Under continuous operation at 90% of the critical power, the structures remained operational for 24 h. The characteristics of microbridges without and with a protective SiO$_x$ layer were compared. The presence of the coating modifies the electrothermal operating regime of the structures and enables estimated temperatures of approximately 500-700 degrees Celsius to be reached.

papers.title: Matrix Samplers and Quantum-Proof Extractors: Their Correspondence and Almost-Optimal Constructions
papers.summary: We establish an equivalence between matrix samplers and quantum-proof randomness extractors. The classical sampler--extractor equivalence is established by a seminal work of Zuckerman (Random Structures & Algorithms, 1997). Using this equivalence, we construct explicit strong matrix samplers with optimal randomness overhead and near-optimal sample complexity via constructing quantum-proof extractors. Specifically for matrix dimension $D$, accuracy $\varepsilon$ and failure probability $δ\leq\varepsilon$, our matrix sampler uses $m+O_α(\log(D/δ))$ random bits and $O_α(\varepsilon^{-2-α}\log^{1+α}(D/δ))$ samples, for any constant $α>0$. Compared with the matrix sampler of Xun and Zuckerman (CCC 2025), our construction has improvements in two aspects. Under the same optimal random seed length, we can replace the $\operatorname{poly} D$ dependence in the number of samples by $O(\log^{1-γ} D)$. Under the same scale of sample size, we can remove their $\log\log D$ factor in the length of the random seed. Our underlying strong quantum-proof extractor has output length $n-O_α(a+\log(1/η))$ and seed length at most $(1+α)\log a+(2+α)\log(1/η)+O_α(1)$ for $n$-bit sources with conditional min-entropy $n-a$ and error $η$. We also obtain strong quantum-proof extractors for every constant entropy rate, for any error as small as $2^{-Ω(n)}$, having optimal seed length $O(\log(n/η))$ and output length $Ω(n)$, improving previous constructions.

papers.title: The Disordered Universe 2025: Features in a $Λ>0$ Universe
papers.summary: A complete understanding of cosmology, from its earliest epoch all the way to the current dark energy dominated era, requires the development of a mathematical framework that incorporates quantum features in an expanding universe. Such a framework, alongside a description of the underlying degrees of freedom, is so far lacking. Several of the pertinent challenges and puzzles already arise upon considering even the most idealised model of an expanding universe --- the de Sitter spacetime and fluctuations thereof. In these lectures, we review some elementary ideas of the de Sitter physics, passing through the representation theory of the de Sitter group, aspects of canonical quantum gravity, all the way to attempts in describing quasi-local features. Throughout, we highlight open problems that motivate ongoing efforts to understand quantum gravity and cosmology in universes with $Λ>0$. These notes are based on a series of lectures held during the La Ricotta Summer School: The Disordered Universe 2025 from 21 July to 1 August 2025.

papers.title: Generative quantum extreme learning machines
papers.summary: Training the circuit of a quantum generative model is hampered by barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially with the number of qubits. In the present work we propose a generative protocol based on the paradigm of quantum extreme learning machines, in which the circuit is never trained. A random latent vector is encoded into a quantum state, evolved with a fixed unitary and measured, and only a linear output layer is trained. The encoding of the latent variable determines the functions available to the model, while the unitary decides which combinations of them are seen by the trained layer. With the help of Pauli propagation we show that for a Clifford unitary each feature is a single product of sines and cosines of the encoded angles, so that a Clifford circuit, even a strongly entangling one, does not create new functions. Doping the circuit with $T$ gates mixes these products and changes the nonstabilizerness of the state, but the space of functions remains the one fixed by the encoding.
